title: ATS Corpus Authority V1
description: A repository owner's declaration of what a corpus may do with the repository's prose, resolved per use rather than as a single permission. Local availability of source text is not authority to extract it (spec Section 16.9, 17.13), so every use starts unknown and only an explicit declaration moves it. A use whose value is unknown MUST NOT inherit allow from another use, from the repository root, or from any default. A declaration binds nine things and none of them has a default: who issued it (principal), why they may speak for the repository (authority_basis), which repository (repository.name, repository.origin, repository.root_commit), at which revision (repository.effective_from_revision), for which uses (uses), over which paths (content), when it was issued (issued_at), when it must be revisited (review_after), and what replaced it (superseded_by, explicitly null while nothing has). A declaration that omits one of these is refused rather than completed.

principal.description: Who issued this declaration. An identity, not a role: `owner`, `operator`, and `the team` name a seat, and a seat cannot be asked to revisit its own declaration, cannot withdraw it, and outlives whoever occupied it. The scheme-qualified `id` makes the difference mechanical.

id.description: A scheme-qualified identity, for example `https://github.com/<account>` or `mailto:<address>`.

kind.description: A service account can hold an identity but cannot exercise the judgment a review date asks for, so which kind of principal signed is recorded rather than assumed.

authority_basis.description: Why this principal may speak for this repository. The kind gates granting; only the statement says why, and an unstated why cannot be checked by the person who has to rely on it.

kind.description: `owner_declared` is the only basis that can grant a use; every other basis can only restrict, so that a consumer cannot authorise itself.

statement.description: The concrete, checkable reason. Not a restatement of the kind.

contributor_identities.description: Every distinct author and committer identity in the repository's history at the effective revision. The evidence behind an ownership claim: a repository carrying an identity the principal does not account for is one the principal cannot speak for alone.

repository.description: Which repository, unambiguously, and at which revision. A directory name is ambiguous the moment two checkouts share it, so the origin remote and the root commit are bound alongside it.

origin.description: The `origin` remote URL, or an explicit null when the repository has none. Null is an answer; an absent key is not.

root_commit.description: The repository's first commit, in full. The only identity that survives renaming the directory, moving it, changing the remote, and having no remote at all. Forty hex digits for a SHA-1 object format and sixty-four for SHA-256; abbreviated ids are refused because an abbreviation is only unique within one repository, which is the ambiguity this field exists to remove.

effective_from_revision.description: The revision this declaration is bound to. A declaration says nothing about revisions before it.

declaration_location.description: Where the declaration is held. `repository` is the destination state: the owner declares in place, in .ats/corpus.json. `pilot_overlay` is an operator-authored declaration held outside the repository while onboarding is in progress. The loader refuses a declaration whose stated location differs from where it was actually found, because an overlay presented as repository-owned authority is exactly the confusion this field prevents.

uses.description: Authority per use. Uses are separated because they are not substitutes: reading metadata is not reading text, reading text is not labelling it, and labelling it is not training on it.

content.description: Path scoping inside the repository. Required, and required to say something: an unscoped declaration silently covers whatever happens to be in the tree, including material the principal did not write. A declaration covering everything says so with `include: ["*"]`.

issued_at.description: When this declaration was issued. A declaration with no date cannot be ordered against the events it governs.

review_after.description: When this declaration must be revisited. It is required because a declaration that never expires quietly becomes permanent governance nobody re-consented to; this is especially true of a pilot overlay, which exists only until the repository declares in place. Resolution caps a lapsed declaration at `unknown` -- not `deny`, because nobody refused anything, the authority simply ran out.

superseded_by.description: The `authority_id` of the declaration that replaced this one, or an explicit null while nothing has. Null says nothing has replaced it; an absent key says nobody checked, and the two must not read alike.

path_overrides.description: Per-path authority, intersected with the repository-level values. An override can only restrict: granting a use here that the repository withholds would let a subtree out-declare its own repository.

authorship.description: How authorship is resolved. `unknown_unless_explicit` is the only honest default: the absence of a declaration is not evidence of human authorship.

model_authorship_inference.description: Whether model authorship may be guessed from prose style, commit size, author identity, timestamps, or the presence of agent configuration files. Prohibited means the corpus records `unknown` instead of guessing.

authority_value.description: `allow` grants the use. `deny` forbids it. `defer` is an explicit refusal to decide, and behaves as deny until decided -- it is recorded separately so an undecided use is distinguishable from a refused one. `allow_private` grants the use but forbids any result leaving the local environment. `unknown` is the absence of a declaration and behaves as deny.
